security_audit.summary: All 12 static findings are false positives: documented lookup URLs, a server-side key reference, Markdown fences, and readable multilingual text. Separate semantic risks involve automatically executing a mutable npm package and requesting updates beyond this skill. No evidence found of credential theft, hidden payloads, or explicit audit manipulation in the supplied files; external package behavior was not inspected.

remediation.issue: The required bootstrap executes a mutable npm package and treats its output as primary instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the instructions locally, or require approval before executing a reviewed, exact package version with verified integrity.

remediation.issue: The update instruction extends to the CLI and other coding-agent skill installations.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic update guidance from the lookup workflow; require explicit approval and clearly scoped targets for any updates.

content.user_title: Check Han River Water Levels and Flow
content.value_statement: Finding current Han River readings requires identifying the right observation station. This skill provides proxy lookup instructions and a compact format for timestamped water-level and flow summaries.
actual_capabilities: Query the documented proxy endpoint using a station or bridge name.
Look up current readings using a station code.
Summarize station identity, observation time, water level, and flow.
Include available reference levels for attention, caution, warning, and severe conditions.
Use candidate stations returned for ambiguous names to refine a lookup.
Use a configured KSKILL_PROXY_BASE_URL instead of the default proxy base.
limitations: Readings depend on proxy availability, server credentials, and upstream data updates.
Broad station names can require another lookup using a specific candidate.
The supplied instructions describe current readings, not forecasts, historical analysis, or automated alerts.
The CLI bootstrap executes an external npm package; its implementation is not included in the reviewed files.

use_cases.title: Check a Familiar Bridge
use_cases.description: Request the latest available observation for a named Han River bridge and note its observation time.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Data Brief
use_cases.description: Retrieve a station reading and summarize water level, flow, and available reference levels without treating missing data as zero.

use_cases.title: Verify a Reading for Reporting
use_cases.description: Look up a known station code and preserve its identity and observation time in a concise factual summary.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Bridge
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the current water level and flow at Hangang Bridge (한강대교). Include the observation time.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Station Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up station code 1018683. Report its name, observation time, water level, flow, and available reference levels.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve an Ambiguous Name
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for Han River stations using 한강. If the name is ambiguous, show the returned candidates and ask me to choose.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Qualified Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve station [stationCode] through my approved proxy. Summarize readings and available thresholds, note missing data, and distinguish observation time from retrieval time.

output_examples.input: Check Hangang Bridge water level and flow.
output_examples.output: Illustrative format, not a live reading: Hangang Bridge, station 1018683. Observation time: [reported time]. Water level: [reported value] m. Flow: [reported value] m^3/s.
The station name matches multiple candidates. Please choose a returned station name or code before I request its current readings.
The latest observation is unavailable. Upstream updates may be delayed; current water level and flow cannot be confirmed.

best_practices: Use a station code when you know it, and verify the returned station identity.
Include observation and retrieval times, and report missing readings explicitly.
Review and approve external CLI execution; keep package updates separate from routine station lookups.
anti_patterns: Treating raw observations as forecasts, official alerts, or proof of personal safety.
Choosing an arbitrary station when the proxy returns multiple candidates.
Running broad update commands merely to retrieve a water-level reading.

faq.question: Which inputs can I use?
faq.answer: Use a station or bridge name, or provide a station code for a more precise lookup.

faq.question: Do I need an HRFCO API key?
faq.answer: The default proxy supplies the upstream key server-side. Users do not need to provide that key.

faq.question: What does the summary include?
faq.answer: It includes station identity, observation time, water level, flow, and any available reference levels.

faq.question: What happens when a station name is ambiguous?
faq.answer: The proxy returns candidate stations. Choose one and repeat the lookup with its name or code.

faq.question: Are readings guaranteed to be current?
faq.answer: No. Upstream updates can be delayed, and the latest ten-minute observation may be missing.

faq.question: Does the skill require running external code?
faq.answer: The entry file requests npm CLI execution. Local instructions also document direct HTTP requests; review external execution before approving it.
